mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% over two consecutive quarters signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS > 2% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not negative in at least 60% of quarters where GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE exceeds 6% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which depresses earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 70% of months where both INDPRO and HOUST decline by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp reduction in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 1% during a recession signals an aggressive monetary easing, which boosts risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during episodes where FEDFUNDS falls below 1% and UNRATE exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong acceleration in personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth > 0.5% month-over-month) combined with rising consumer spending (RSAFS growth > 0.4% month-over-month) signals robust demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS MoM growth > 0.5% AND RSAFS MoM growth > 0.4%
failure_condition: If S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in at least 65% of months where both PAYEMS and RSAFS accelerate above their respective thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% for six consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as discount rates rise.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods when UNRATE remains below 4% for six consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% combined with stagnant real GDP growth (GDPC1 YoY change < 1%) signals inflation without growth, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative in at least 60% of quarters where CPIAUCSL rises above 3% YoY and GDPC1 grows less than 1% YoY.
